prompt: Match each person to the way the lesson says they have a stake in the delivery dashboard.
hint: Decides, influences, is affected, provides the data.

pairs.right: Decides: agrees to the hours spent
Influences: the carriers' contracts are his
Is affected: opens it every morning
Provides the data: builds the pipelines

prompt: Why did the store managers become stakeholders in a dashboard about warehouse deliveries?

choices.text: Because they will use the dashboard every day to dispatch vans
choices.why: Dispatching is Marcos's work; most store managers never touch a van.

choices.text: Part of their bonus depends on the KPI
choices.why: Right: from that day the number was their pay, not something they read.

choices.text: Because Helena asked for every manager to be invited
choices.why: Nobody invited them; that is why the lesson calls them the ones nobody listed.

choices.text: Because they provide the delivery data
choices.why: The data comes from the ERP and the carriers, through Tiago's pipelines.

prompt: In its last week, a project finds that the carriers' file arrives only on Fridays. Which stakeholder was left out of the planning?

choices.text: The owner of the KPI, who should have asked for daily data
choices.why: Caio can ask for daily data; only the people who produce it know whether it exists.

choices.text: The CEO, who approves the budget
choices.why: Helena's approval does not change when a file arrives.

choices.text: Whoever provides the data
choices.why: Right: the one most often forgotten, because they neither use nor decide.

choices.text: The daily users, who would have noticed at launch
choices.why: They would notice at launch, which is exactly too late.

prompt: To find a missing stakeholder, follow the ___: for each indicator, ask who is judged, paid or blamed by it.
hint: The first of the three checks.

prompt: What does the lesson recommend for stakeholders with high power and low interest, such as Helena?
hint: They can stop the project but will not follow it.

choices.text: Invite them to every project meeting
choices.why: That is for "manage closely"; it wastes the time of someone who does not want the detail.

choices.text: Short, rare updates, and no surprises
choices.why: Right: answer their question briefly and never let them find out late.

choices.text: Monitor them now and then
choices.why: Monitoring is for low power; Helena can cancel the project with one sentence.

choices.text: Ask them to review the mock of every view
choices.why: The mock goes to the people who will live with the view.

prompt: Why does the lesson place Tiago in "manage closely" although he has no formal authority?
hint: What happens to the project if the data does not arrive?

choices.text: Because he is a contractor and could leave
choices.why: His contract is not the argument; what the pipelines deliver is.

choices.text: Because data engineers always outrank analysts
choices.why: No rank is involved; the lesson says he has no formal authority.

choices.text: Because he is the one who will use the dashboard most
choices.why: Marcos is the daily user; Tiago is not a user at all.

choices.text: Without his data, nothing else on the map saves the project
choices.why: Right: power is the ability to change the course, and refusing what it needs is one way.

prompt: Varanda announces that next year the carriers' contracts will be renewed on the dashboard's numbers. What should Lívia do with the map?

choices.text: Redraw it: the carriers' interest and their weight have both just risen
choices.why: Right: the same move as the store managers, for the same reason; something about the number changed.

choices.text: Nothing: the carriers are outside the company
choices.why: A stakeholder is anybody the number touches, inside or out.

choices.text: Send the map to the carriers so they know where they stand
choices.why: The map is a working note; labelling someone "monitor" is not something to circulate.

choices.text: Move them to "keep satisfied", since their power is now final
choices.why: Their interest rose most; "keep satisfied" is for people who will not follow the project.

prompt: The power-interest map is a working ___ for the analyst and the project owner, not a document to circulate.
Match each reader to the view of the delivery KPI the lesson gives them.

pairs.right: One number and its trend, monthly
Today's orders at risk, as a list
His store against the others, by kind

right_distractors: Every store ranked on the bare total

prompt: What must stay the same across the four views, by the lesson?
hint: Otherwise you are back at lesson 1's meeting.

choices.text: The level of detail
choices.why: Detail is exactly what changes, from one number to order by order.

choices.text: The definition of the KPI
choices.why: Right: four views of one definition are safe; four definitions are four numbers with one name.

choices.text: How often it is read
choices.why: Frequency follows each reader's decision: monthly for Helena, several times a day for Marcos.

choices.text: The chart type, so readers can compare their pages
choices.why: Marcos's view is a list with no chart at all.

prompt: Why does Marcos's view carry no on-time rate at all?

choices.text: Because he has no authority to act on the KPI
choices.why: He acts all day; on orders, not on a rate.

choices.text: Because rates are too hard to read on the warehouse floor
choices.why: Readability is not the reason; the rate answers the wrong question for him.

choices.text: Rates sum up finished orders; his are on the road
choices.why: Right: his question is which orders need him now.

choices.text: Because the rate is computed only once a month
choices.why: Caio reads it weekly; frequency is not what rules it out.

prompt: Which questions does the lesson ask about a reader before anything is drawn? Choose all that apply.
hint: Four of them, and the answers are the specification.

choices.text: What decision they make with it
choices.why: Right: the first question, as in every lesson of this course.

choices.text: Where they are when they read it
choices.why: Right: a phone before a meeting is not a desk on Monday.

choices.text: Which BI tool they prefer
choices.why: The tool draws the answer; it does not decide the view.

choices.text: How much detail that decision needs
choices.why: Right: Helena one number, Marcos order by order.

choices.text: What colour scheme their department uses
choices.why: A matter of layout, not of what the view must answer.

prompt: Put the steps of building one stakeholder's view in the lesson's order.
items: Show a mock with invented numbers
Confirm the requirement in a short note
Connect the data and build it
trap: Building first and showing the result is the order a finished dashboard pays for with a month of rework.

prompt: Why does the lesson tell Lívia not to open with "what do you want on the dashboard?"
hint: What kind of answer does that question get?

choices.text: It takes too long to answer in half an hour
choices.why: It is answered quickly; the problem is what the answer contains.

choices.text: It gets charts seen elsewhere
choices.why: Right: asking about their work and decisions gets the requirement instead.

choices.text: Stakeholders resent being asked about tools
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson is about resentment.

choices.text: The analyst should decide the content and present it finished
choices.why: The opposite: the content comes from the person's decisions, and the mock comes before the build.

prompt: Renata wants the headline to be deliveries within two days; Caio wants delivered on promise. What is Lívia's job?
hint: Not to pick the winner, and not to average.

choices.text: Pick the stricter definition, since it protects the customer
choices.why: The choice is not the analyst's; and the stricter one punishes furniture for a promise nobody made.

choices.text: Show both as the headline, side by side
choices.why: Two headlines under one name are lesson 1's meeting again.

choices.text: Set out both, with their numbers, for Caio to decide
choices.why: Right: Caio owns delivery, he chose, and Renata's figure went to her page as a labelled metric.

choices.text: Average 50% and 83.3% into one figure everyone accepts
choices.why: An average of two definitions is a third number with no definition at all.

prompt: Before any data is connected, Lívia shows each person a ___ of their view, with invented numbers labelled as invented.
hint: A drawing on paper or in a slide.

prompt: Bruno sees the first version of the stores' page: every store ranked on the bare on-time total, Contagem near the bottom. What did the project miss?

choices.text: A page with more stores on it
choices.why: More rows on the same bare total change nothing.

choices.text: A faster refresh of the delivery data, every hour
choices.why: Freshness is not the problem; the comparison is.

choices.text: Talking to him, and comparing by kind of delivery
choices.why: Right: an affected stakeholder would have pointed at the mix, which is what the bare total measures.

choices.text: Moving him to the "monitor" quadrant
choices.why: With his pay on the line he belongs further up and to the right.

prompt: After an interview, Lívia sends Marcos a note. What goes in it?
hint: So both sides can point at the same thing.

choices.text: The decision, the definition, the detail, the frequency and what is left out
choices.why: Right: it turns a conversation each side remembers differently into a document.

choices.text: A thank-you and the date of the launch
choices.why: Polite, and it records nothing either side can point at later.

choices.text: His quadrant on the power-interest map
choices.why: The map is not shared with the people on it.

choices.text: The SQL that will produce his view
choices.why: He needs what the view answers, not how it is built.

prompt: Six months after Caio chose delivered on promise, Renata asks again why her two-day figure is not the headline. What does the lesson say saves the argument?

choices.text: Helena overruling her
choices.why: Escalating again repeats the argument; the decision already exists.

choices.text: A written record of the decision
choices.why: Right: the page with both definitions and the decision is the answer.

choices.text: Removing the two-day figure from her page
choices.why: It is a fair metric for parcels; hiding it would start a new argument.

choices.text: Lívia remembering the original meeting clearly
choices.why: Memories differ, which is the reason to write it down.
